phrases.en: In the house lives John
By the tree lies a book
Under the bed sits a cat
The Chair and the Books

phrases.sw: John aliweka kiti juu ya meza ili afikie kitabu kilichokuwa juu ya rafu. Anna aliweka paka juu ya kiti. Paka aliweka mguu juu ya kitabu. Kitabu kilianguka chini ya kiti. Kiti kilianguka chini ya meza. John alisema: wakati ujao nitamwomba Grace.
phrases.en: John put a chair on the table to reach a book on the shelf. Anna put the cat on the chair. The cat put its paw on the book. The book fell under the chair. The chair fell under the table. John said: next time I will ask Grace.
The Magical Night

phrases.sw: Usiku mmoja vitu vyote ndani ya nyumba ya Anna vilibadilisha mahali pake. Kitanda kilikuwa jikoni. Meza ilikuwa bustanini. Vitabu vilining'inia juu ya mlango. Anna alitembea kutoka chumba kimoja hadi kingine na hakuelewa kilichokuwa kikiendelea. Katika chumba cha mwisho alikuwa ameketi paka, akitazama ukutani. Anna alipomwangalia kiti — kiti kilipanda polepole na kuning'inia chini ya dari. Paka hakugeuka.
phrases.en: One night all the objects in Anna's house changed their places. The bed was in the kitchen. The table was in the garden. The books were hanging above the door. Anna walked from room to room and could not understand what was happening. In the last room sat the cat, staring at the wall. When Anna looked at the chair — the chair slowly rose and hung under the ceiling. The cat did not turn around.
The Lost Glasses

phrases.sw: Grace alitafuta miwani yake. Haikuwa juu ya meza, wala chini ya meza, wala ndani ya mfuko, wala kati ya vitabu. Alimpigia John simu. John aliuliza: umeitazama kichwani? Grace aliweka simu chini.
phrases.en: Grace was looking for her glasses. They were not on the table, not under the table, not in the bag, not between the books. She called John. John asked: have you looked on your head? Grace put the phone down.
One Pen

phrases.sw: Daniel alileta vitabu vitano, daftari tatu na kalamu moja. Anna alisema: kalamu moja haitoshi kwa watu watano. Daniel alisema: nilikula moja njiani. Anna alishangaa na akaamua kutouliza tena.
phrases.en: Daniel brought five books, three notebooks and one pen. Anna said: one pen is not enough for five people. Daniel said: I ate one on the way. Anna was surprised and decided not to ask any more questions.
Anna's House

phrases.sw: John alimweleza Grace mahali anapoishi Anna. Karibu na mti mkubwa. Kati ya soko na shule. Mbali na mto. Karibu na msikiti. Grace alisikiliza kwa saa moja. Kisha alisema: ninamjua Anna miaka ishirini. Mimi mwenyewe ndiye niliyekuleta kwake.
phrases.en: John was explaining to Grace where Anna lives. Near the big tree. Between the market and the school. Far from the river. Close to the mosque. Grace listened for an hour. Then she said: I have known Anna for twenty years. I am the one who brought you to her myself.

moderator_questions.sw: Swali la 1. Kitenzi na kitu kama mtenda
moderator_questions.en: Question 1. The verb and an object as subject

body.sw:
Angalia sentensi ulizotafsiri:

- "Meza inasimama ukutani"
- "Kitabu kilalalo juu ya meza"
- "Mti unakua karibu na nyumba"

Na uzilinganishe na sentensi ambapo mtenda ni mtu:

- "John anaenda nyumbani"
- "Anna anakula mkate"

Katika lugha yako — je kitenzi kinabadilika umbo lake kulingana na ni nani mtenda? Au umbo la kitenzi ni sawa kwa mtu na kwa kitu?
body.en:
Look at the phrases you translated:

- "The table stands by the wall"
- "The book lies on the table"
- "The tree grows by the house"

And compare them with phrases where the subject is a person:

- "John is going home"
- "Anna is eating bread"

In your language — does the verb change its form depending on who the subject is? Or is the verb form the same for a person and for an object?

sw: Sawa — kitenzi hakibadiliki iwe mtenda ni mtu au kitu
Tofauti — kuna tofauti → tofauti iko wapi hasa? Toa mfano: "John anasimama" na "meza inasimama" — kitenzi kinaonekana vipi katika kila kisa?
en: The same — the verb does not change whether the subject is a person or an object
Different — there is a difference → what exactly is the difference? Give an example: "John stands" and "the table stands" — what does the verb look like in each case?

follow_up.sw:
Kama kinabadilika — angalia vitu vyote ulivyotafsiri (meza, kitabu, mti, maziwa, ng'ombe). Je kitenzi ni sawa kwa vitu vyote au kila kitu kina umbo lake la kitenzi?

- Sawa kwa vitu vyote
- Vitu tofauti vina maumbo tofauti ya kitenzi → toa mfano kwa kila kitu
follow_up.en:
If it changes — look at all the objects you translated (table, book, tree, milk, cow). Is the verb the same for all objects or does each object have its own verb form?

- The same for all objects
- Different objects have different verb forms → give an example for each object

body.sw:
Katika Kirusi "John na Anna wanaenda" — kitenzi kiko katika wingi bila kujali kwamba kuna mwanaume mmoja na mwanamke mmoja.

Katika lugha yako — nini kinatokea kwa kitenzi wakati watenda ni wengi? Angalia sentensi "John na Anna wanaenda nyumbani" uliyoitafsiri.
body.en:
In Russian "John and Anna are going" — the verb is in the plural regardless of the fact that there is one man and one woman.

In your language — what happens to the verb when there are several subjects? Look at the phrase "John and Anna are going home" that you translated.

sw: Kitenzi kinakwenda tu katika wingi
Kitenzi kinapatana na mtenda wa karibu zaidi
Kitenzi kinachukua umbo maalum kwa mtenda wa pamoja → toa mifano
en: The verb simply goes into the plural
The verb agrees with the nearest subject
The verb takes a special form for a compound subject → give examples

follow_up.sw:
Sasa angalia sentensi "meza na kitabu viko chumbani". Je kitenzi kinafanya kama na watu wawili — au tofauti?

- Sawa
- Tofauti → tofauti iko wapi hasa? Toa mfano
follow_up.en:
Now look at the phrase "the table and the book are in the room". Does the verb behave the same way as with two people — or differently?

- The same
- Differently → how exactly? Give an example

body.sw:
Katika Kirusi "moja" inapatana na nomino kwa jinsia: один стол (meza moja, kiume) / одна книга (kitabu kimoja, kike) / одно дерево (mti mmoja, kati). Inafanya kama kivumishi.

Katika Kiingereza "one" haibadiliki kabisa — one table / one book / one tree.

Katika Kiswahili "moja" pia inabadilika lakini kulingana na ngeli ya nomino — kitabu kimoja / mtu mmoja.

Angalia tafsiri zako za sentensi zenye "moja":

- Mwanaume mmoja anaenda nyumbani
- Mwanamke mmoja anaenda nyumbani
- Kitabu kimoja kilalalo mezani
- Mti mmoja unakua karibu na nyumba
- Ng'ombe mmoja anasimama uwanjani

Je neno "moja" ni sawa katika sentensi hizi zote au linabadilika?
body.en:
In Russian "one" agrees with the noun by gender: один стол (one table, masculine) / одна книга (one book, feminine) / одно дерево (one tree, neuter). It behaves like an adjective.

In English "one" does not change at all — one table / one book / one tree.

In Swahili "one" also changes but by the noun class of the noun — kitabu kimoja (one book) / mtu mmoja (one person).

Look at your translations of the phrases with "one":

- One man is going home
- One woman is going home
- One book is lying on the table
- One tree is growing by the house
- One cow is standing in the yard

Is the word "one" the same in all these phrases or does it change?

sw: Sawa — haibadiliki kabisa
Inabadilika → inabadilika kwa nini (kwa jinsia, kwa ngeli ya nomino, kwa kitu kingine)? Andika maumbo yote uliyoyapata
en: The same — it does not change at all
It changes → what does it change by (by gender, by noun class, by something else)? Write out all the forms you ended up with

moderator_questions.sw: Swali la 4. Tofauti ndogo za mahali

body.sw:
Katika Kiswahili kuna njia tatu tofauti za kusema "kuwepo mahali fulani":

- niko — nipo mahali fulani (kwa takriban, si kwa usahihi): "niko nyumbani" = mahali fulani ndani ya nyumba
- nipo — nipo hapa hasa (msemaji anaonyesha sehemu maalum): "nipo hapa"
- nimo — nipo ndani ya kitu: "nimo ndani ya nyumba"

Katika Kirusi hakuna tofauti kama hiyo — "я в доме" (niko ndani ya nyumba) inafunika hali zote, bila kujali kama ni kwa usahihi au kwa takriban, ndani au nje.

Katika lugha yako — je kuna tofauti ndogo kama hizo za mahali?
body.en:
In Swahili there are three different ways to say "to be somewhere":

- niko — I am somewhere (approximately, not precisely): "I am home" = somewhere in the house
- nipo — I am exactly here (the speaker is pointing to a specific spot): "I am right here"
- nimo — I am inside something: "I am inside the house"

In Russian there is no such distinction — "я в доме" (I am in the house) covers everything, regardless of whether it is precise or approximate, inside or outside.

In your language — are there such fine distinctions for location?

sw: Hapana — neno moja au umbo moja kwa hali zote
Ndiyo — kuna tofauti → tofauti iko wapi hasa? Tunga mifano katika lugha yako na utoe tafsiri kwa Kiswahili na Kiingereza
en: No — one word or form for all situations
Yes — there is a distinction → what exactly? Formulate examples in your language and provide a translation in Swahili and English

body.sw:
Katika Kiswahili unaweza kusema:

Mezani pana chakula — Kuna chakula mezani

Hapa kitenzi pana kina kiambishi awali pa- — alama ya mahali hasa. Kwa hiyo si tu "kuna chakula" bali "hasa pale kuna chakula" — mahali pamekuwa sehemu ya kitenzi chenyewe.

Katika Kirusi hii haipo — "на столе стоит стакан" (glasi inasimama mezani) — kitenzi "inasimama" hakibadiliki kabisa kwa sababu mtenda yuko mezani.

Angalia tafsiri zako za sentensi kama:

- "Juu ya meza kuna glasi"
- "Ndani ya nyumba anaishi John"
- "Karibu na mti kilalalo kitabu"

Katika lugha yako — je kitenzi kinabadilika kwa njia yoyote katika sentensi kama hizi ikilinganishwa na za kawaida? Au umbo la kitenzi ni sawa kabisa?
body.en:
In Swahili you can say:

Mezani pana chakula — There is food on the table

Here the verb pana contains the prefix pa- — a marker of exact location. So it is not just "there is food" but "right there there is food" — the location has become part of the verb itself.

In Russian this does not exist — "на столе стоит стакан" (a glass stands on the table) — the verb "stands" does not change at all because of the fact that the subject is on the table.

Look at your translations of phrases like:

- "On the table stands a glass"
- "In the house lives John"
- "By the tree lies a book"

In your language — does the verb change in any way in such sentences compared to ordinary ones? Or is the verb form exactly the same?

sw: Sawa kabisa — mahali hayaathiri kitenzi
Inabadilika → inabadilika vipi hasa? Toa mifano na utoe tafsiri kwa Kiswahili na Kiingereza
en: Exactly the same — location does not affect the verb
It changes → how exactly? Give examples and provide a translation in Swahili and English

body.en: Based on all the content provided — translations of phrases and answers to the questions above — write a short grammar reference on agreement in your language.

sw: Upatanisho wa kitenzi na mtenda — inabadilika kwa nini (nafsi, nambari, jinsia, ngeli, au haibadiliki)
Kitenzi na kitu kama mtenda — sawa na mtu au tofauti
Mtenda wa pamoja — nini kinatokea kwa kitenzi
Nambari — zinabadilika au la, zinabadilika kwa nini, mpangilio, maneno ya kuhesabu kama yapo
Nambari "moja" — inafanya vipi
Kuonyesha mahali — kihusishi, kihusishi cha nyuma, hali, chembe
Tofauti kati ya "wapi" na "kwenda wapi" — inavyoonyeshwa
Tofauti ndogo za mahali — kama zipo
Mahali na umbo la kitenzi — kunaathiri au la
Mifano ya sentensi kwa kila kanuni

Expressing location — preposition, postposition, case, particle
